 A heli count was done by the Toboggan Creek Hatchery on August 17 between the Morice River junction to Bulkley Falls for a total 711. Visibility during the assessment flight was excellent. Over 67% occupied the section of river from Perow downstream to Knockholt. Very few spawners were found in the Richfield Creek section which is usually a major spawning area. As in pervious years a comparative ground count was done in the vicinity of McQuarrie and Richfield Creeks. The ground survey suggested that few chinook were missed by the aerial count resulting in an estimate of 770. The physical condition of the fish appeared to be fairly good with few prespawn mortalities being observed. 217 different chinook were sampled 78% were wild, 22% adipose clipped & 60% were male. Typically Bulkley chinook are five year olds, although survival from the 2001 brood of 5600 (highest recorded escapement) appears poor. The 2001 brood did not come back well as four year olds either. Toboggan Creek Hatchery summary:
Chinook assessment was carried out in conjunction with egg takes, including a helicopter count of salmon spawners on Aug. 18. A total of only 150 chinook were observed between the Morice River junction and the Bulkley Falls, with over 65% occupying the section of river from the Richfield Creek confluence downstream to the McQuarrie Creek groundwater area. Four chinook were observed upstream of the falls at the Foxy Creek / Maxan Creek confluence. Very few spawners were found in the lower end of the river this year. It is possible that many of the chinook that entered the river early (prior to the extremely hot weather in July and early August) did not survive to spawn, and may have been removed by predators due to a lethargic state of awareness. Visibility during the assessment flight was excellent. Chinook were easily counted in the pools, as well as on the spawning riffles, due to the very good light conditions. As in previous years, we did a comparative ground count in the vicinity of McQuarrie and Richfield Creeks to verify the accuracy of the aerial count. Few, if any, chinook were missed in this year's flight. From these observations, and incorporating the ground count carried out during the same period, it is estimated that the live chinook escapement present in the upper Bulkley River during the time of the count was approximately 160 adults.

Cedar River - 726; Hadenschild Creek - 23; Anweiller Creek - 41 = 790 chinook for the final estimate for 2005.
The main river estimate is based maintly on the Aug. 12 count of 330 redds = 660 adults, plus 10% for under counting =726. Redd overlapping as seen in 2004 was not observed this year and therefore no correction on the estimate as per 2004.
The Hadenschild estimate is based on the one count as none were seen on the first count. 18 were counted x 1.25 (estimate 25% of stock could not be counted) = 23.
The Anweiller estimate is based on a count of 15 redds = 30 adults, plus 35% more for area of stream that cannot be seen from the air = 41.

Walked a 1km section of Anweiller and counted 100 live and 55 redds in a section where only 7 chinook had been counted from the air. Hadenschild was not inspected as the habitat has changed there limiting chinook spawning. The final estimate is for the main Cedar River and Anweiller Creek combined.
